title: BLD-684: CLI --json Flag for Machine-Parseable Comment Output
description: This tour walks through the addition of a --json flag to the `hlx comments list` command in helix-cli. The host agent runner inside a sprite needs to pull unprocessed comments programmatically via execFile, but the existing output was human-readable text that omitted comment IDs. Adding --json enables the runner to parse structured comment data (including IDs for cursor-based deduplication via lastProcessedCommentId) without breaking existing human-readable output for operators.

steps.description: The `hlx comments list` command already supported `--since` filtering and `--helix-only`, but all output was formatted as human-readable text: `[timestamp] Author [markers]: content`. The runner in helix-global-server calls `hlx` via execFile and needs structured output it can parse. Critically, the human-readable format omitted the comment `id` field, which the runner needs to advance the `lastProcessedCommentId` cursor on the server for idempotent deduplication. This file is the sole change target in helix-cli for BLD-684.
steps.title: Overview: Why This File Needed Changing

steps.description: The `CommentResponse` type (imported or defined around this line) already includes an `id: string` field along with `author`, `content`, `isHelixTagged`, `isAgentAuthored`, and `createdAt`. No schema changes were needed — the data was always there, just never surfaced in output. This means `JSON.stringify(comments)` will naturally include comment IDs without any transformation logic.
steps.title: CommentResponse Type Already Has id

steps.description: The `--json` flag is parsed here using the existing `getFlag()` utility, consistent with how `--since` and `--helix-only` are already parsed. No new infrastructure is needed. The flag is boolean — its presence triggers JSON output mode. This keeps the change minimal and non-breaking: the default code path (no --json) is completely unchanged.
steps.title: Parsing the --json Flag

steps.description: Client-side filtering (`--since` timestamp comparison and `--helix-only`) is applied to the fetched comments array before the output branch. This is important: both the JSON path and the human-readable path operate on the same filtered dataset. The runner can safely combine `--since <marker> --json` to get only new, unprocessed comments in structured form — the same semantics it would rely on for incremental polling.
steps.title: Filtering Applied Before Both Output Paths

steps.description: When `--json` is specified, `JSON.stringify(comments)` is written to stdout and the function returns early. The full filtered array is serialized, including all fields: `id`, `author`, `content`, `isHelixTagged`, `isAgentAuthored`, `createdAt`. The runner's execFile call captures this stdout, parses it, and uses the `id` fields to track `lastProcessedCommentId`. The early return ensures the human-readable loop below never executes in this branch.
steps.title: JSON Output Branch with Early Return

steps.description: The original `[timestamp] Author [markers]: content` formatting loop is completely untouched. It only executes when `--json` is not passed, preserving backwards compatibility for human operators using the CLI interactively. No existing scripts or workflows that parse the human-readable format are affected. This satisfies the acceptance criterion: default output is preserved, --json is purely additive.
steps.title: Human-Readable Output Path Unchanged

steps.description: The code review artifact confirms the implementation is complete and correct. All acceptance criteria are met: --json flag parsed at L18, JSON.stringify output includes all fields including `id` at L40, filtering applied before output, human-readable default preserved, and no breaking changes. The review explicitly verified that comment IDs are included in JSON output for cursor-based deduplication — the core requirement from the runner's perspective. No follow-up changes were required.
steps.title: Code Review: No Issues Found

steps.description: The complete data flow is now: (1) Runner calls `hlx comments list --since <lastProcessedCommentId marker> --json` via execFile. (2) CLI fetches all comments from `GET /tickets/{ticketId}/comments`, filters by --since and --helix-only, then outputs JSON array to stdout. (3) Runner parses JSON, processes each comment, and advances lastProcessedCommentId using the `id` field. This closes the pull loop described in the diagnosis. The change is minimal (one flag, one branch in list.ts), non-breaking, and directly unblocks the host agent series (BLD-681 through BLD-684) by giving the runner structured access to the comment stream.
steps.title: Summary: Data Flow Through the Full Pull Loop
